sentences: I measure the hardness of the mineral by scratching it against a set of reference plates.
I check the streak color by rubbing the specimen across an unglazed porcelain plate.
I observe the luster of the sample and record whether it appears metallic or nonmetallic.
I note the cleavage directions and the angles between them on the broken crystal.
I examine the fracture surface to see if it is conchoidal, uneven, or splintery.
I determine the specific gravity by weighing the mineral in air and then in water.
I test the mineral's reaction to dilute hydrochloric acid by placing a drop on it.
I inspect the crystal system by measuring the interfacial angles with a goniometer.
I check for magnetism by holding a small magnet near the powdered sample.
I record the color of the mineral in both natural light and under a fluorescent lamp.
I look for twinning by examining the crystal under a polarizing microscope.
I test the tenacity by attempting to bend a thin sliver of the mineral.
I measure the electrical conductivity of the specimen using a simple multimeter.
I observe the fluorescence by placing the mineral under an ultraviolet lamp.
I check the radioactivity with a Geiger counter held close to the rock surface.
I determine the solubility by stirring a small amount of powder into warm water.
I note the habit of the crystal, whether it is prismatic, tabular, or acicular.
I examine the mineral for pseudomorphism after comparing it to a known reference.
I record the optical properties by rotating the thin section between crossed polarizers.
I check the piezoelectricity by applying pressure to the crystal and measuring the charge.
